objects.original: Original r independent standard d-dimensional Gaussian columns with product law mu, their physical rows gamma_i, exact source cosine t_i and closed rowwise truncated matrices Y_i with Gaussian-first tensor indices.
objects.reconstructed: The fixed objects are D = R^d, E = R^(q+1), the sample space Ω = {0,...,q} → D, the finite product standard Gaussian measure μ, the real scalar r = q+1, the real scalars L and C, angles θ_i, deterministic cosine vectors t_i, coordinate-row random vectors x_i, and random real matrices Y_i indexed in both directions by {0,...,q} × {0,...,q}. The vector x_i is precisely the Euclidean vector with coordinates ω(b)_i; the WithLp wrappers do not change those coordinates. The outer products and Kronecker product have the paired-index ordering stated in the reconstructed theorem.
objects.evidence: Decoder entry expansion at ((b,k),(c,l)) is d inverse times gamma_b gamma_c t_k t_l, matching source C2p1/Ex107 and literal code. One row-map name change preserves the original column sample space.

domains.original: Natural d,q with 2q+1<d and r=q+1, including q=0; rows 1 through d and degrees zero through q; real Euclidean vectors and r-squared real square matrices.
domains.reconstructed: The parameters d and q are natural numbers, including zero before the hypothesis is imposed. The hypothesis forces d ≥ 2q+2; q = 0 is allowed. Coordinate indices i range from 0 through d−1. Indices b,c,k,l range from 0 through q, including both endpoints. Samples ω belong to Ω. The vectors x_i and t_i lie in E; Y_i has (q+1)^2 rows and columns and real entries. All scalar formulas use the usual embedding of natural numbers into R. Euclidean norms are used for vectors, and the complete Euclidean operator norm is used for matrix Bochner integrability.
domains.evidence: Zero-based Fin indices correspond exactly to original physical i.val+1; theta i.val+1-1/2 equals the original half-grid. Natural q includes zero and hq implies d>=2. No q-positive or dimension-square restriction appears.

quantifiers.original: For every allowed d,q and every physical i, the actual matrix square is integrable; the sum of its expectations over all physical rows has the deterministic PSD upper bound.
quantifiers.reconstructed: For every pair of natural numbers d and q satisfying 2q+1 < d, form all displayed objects by their fixed definitions. The first conclusion holds for every i in {0,...,d−1}. The second conclusion concerns the finite sum over that same entire index set. Positive semidefiniteness includes symmetry and the nonnegative quadratic-form condition for every real vector indexed by {0,...,q} × {0,...,q}. No constant, truncation level, angle, or vector is existentially chosen.
quantifiers.evidence: The explicit per-row universal integrability and entire physical-row sum match the two conjuncts. Neither a pointwise event nor a free threshold/constant is introduced.

assumptions.original: The source range is the sole explicit proposition. The law, rows, features and local cutoff are definitions. Gaussian moment, row transport, frame, integrability and PSD facts are internal proof ingredients.
assumptions.reconstructed: The sole mathematical hypothesis on the parameters is the strict inequality 2q+1 < d. The Gaussian law, product sample measure, cosine vectors, truncation level, and matrices are definitions, not additional hypotheses. Integrability is an asserted output. The condition ||x_i(ω)||_2^2 ≤ L is the branch condition defining Y_i at each sample, including equality; it is not an assumption that samples satisfy that condition.
assumptions.evidence: The same sole hq survives exact code/type comparison. Row law, R4, actual majorant integrability and shared PSD residual application are supplied in the whole body; their existence is never moved into binders.

conclusion.original: Ex115-117 bound sum_i E_mu[Y_i squared] by 2r(r+2)/d times I_(r squared). Genuine integrability of each ordinary matrix square is the source-implicit expectation obligation, made explicit as an output.
conclusion.reconstructed: For each i, the matrix-valued function ω ↦ Y_i(ω)Y_i(ω), with ordinary matrix multiplication, is Bochner integrable against μ: it is almost everywhere strongly measurable and the integral of its operator norm is finite. In addition, C times the identity matrix minus the sum over all i of the Bochner integrals of Y_i(ω)Y_i(ω) is a real symmetric positive semidefinite matrix. Equivalently, the sum of these matrix second moments is at most C times the identity in the positive-semidefinite order. This is a deterministic order statement about integrated matrix squares, not a pointwise or probability bound. The explicit integrability assertion ensures these are integrable Bochner integrals rather than reliance on totalized nonintegrable integrals.
conclusion.evidence: Frozen raw p14 Ex113-117 and full source map support the actual uncentered endpoint. Integrability is an internal source-implicit analytic conclusion, not strengthened hypotheses. Full PSD includes symmetry.

scopes.original: One original unconditional column-product law for every row; each inclusive R_i<=L cutoff separately; ordinary matrix squares and full Hermitian/quadratic PSD after actual Bochner integration in Euclidean operator norm; no centered or weighted-centered claim.
scopes.reconstructed: The universal parameter quantifiers and their strict dimension hypothesis enclose every local definition and both conjuncts of the conclusion. One common Ω and μ is used for all i. The angles and cosine vectors are deterministic; x_i and Y_i depend on ω. The truncation branch applies separately to each i and ω, using the squared norm of that row, with the zero matrix on the complementary event ||x_i(ω)||_2^2 > L. In the second conclusion, each product Y_i(ω)Y_i(ω) is integrated before the finite sum is taken. The identity has the paired index set {0,...,q} × {0,...,q}. No almost-sure qualifier weakens the resulting deterministic matrix order assertion.
scopes.evidence: Closed per-row event and unconditional mu are literal in decoder/code/source; matrix multiplication is ordinary. V2 author scope now names only the uncentered PSD estimate; absent centered T and p15 are explicitly excluded.

constant_dependencies.original: Exact r=q+1, L=2r+3 log(1000d), source half-grid, constant-feature normalization one and positive-degree sqrt(2), and coefficient 2r(r+2)/d. No unspecified absolute C from main Lemma4.4 is asserted.
constant_dependencies.reconstructed: The scalar r = q+1 depends only on q. The truncation level is exactly L = 2r + 3 log(1000d), with natural logarithm, and depends only on d and q. The bound is exactly C = 2r(r+2)/d, depending only on d and q. The numbers 2, 3, and 1000, the factor sqrt(2), the half-grid shift 1/2, and π are fixed constants. The angles θ_i depend only on i and d; the cosine coordinate t_i(k) is fixed by i,k,d, with k ranging through 0,...,q. No scalar constant depends on ω or is left unspecified.
constant_dependencies.evidence: Decoder yields identical L and C=2(q+1)(q+3)/d, exact source coefficient. Current formula and code retain d inverse squared in the majorant before frame reduction; no kappa or sample-dependent constant.
